COMPUTER STUDIES MARCH — TERMLY EXAM #17
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: COMPUTER STUDIES MARCH
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When learning Emerging Technologies, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Emerging Technologies.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Emerging Technologies.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Emerging Technologies.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Emerging Technologies.

2. When learning Cybersecurity, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Cybersecurity.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Cybersecurity.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Cybersecurity.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Cybersecurity.

3. ICT stands for: (1 mark)
   A. International Cricket Team
   B. Input Cable Tester
   C. Internal Cooking Timer
   D. Information and Communication Technology

4. When learning Professional Ethics and Legal Issues in Computing, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Professional Ethics and Legal Issues in Computing.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Professional Ethics and Legal Issues in Computing.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Professional Ethics and Legal Issues in Computing.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Professional Ethics and Legal Issues in Computing.

5. When learning Data Analysis and Visualisation, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Data Analysis and Visualisation.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Data Analysis and Visualisation.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Data Analysis and Visualisation.
   D. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Data Analysis and Visualisation.

6. When learning Social and Ethical Issues in Networking, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Social and Ethical Issues in Networking.
   B. Skip safety briefings for Social and Ethical Issues in Networking.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Social and Ethical Issues in Networking.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Social and Ethical Issues in Networking.

7. When learning Artificial Intelligence Implications and Ethics, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Artificial Intelligence Implications and Ethics.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Artificial Intelligence Implications and Ethics.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Artificial Intelligence Implications and Ethics.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Artificial Intelligence Implications and Ethics.

8. Electricity safety rule: (1 mark)
   A. Insert metal objects into sockets for fun
   B. Never touch live wires with wet hands
   C. Overload every socket
   D. Ignore burnt cables

9. When learning Network Troubleshooting, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Network Troubleshooting.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Network Troubleshooting.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Network Troubleshooting.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Network Troubleshooting.

10. When learning Artificial Intelligence Concepts, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Artificial Intelligence Concepts.
   B. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Artificial Intelligence Concepts.
   C. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Artificial Intelligence Concepts.
   D. Skip safety briefings for Artificial Intelligence Concepts.

11. Before using a sharp tool in a workshop, you should: (1 mark)
   A. Remove all guards
   B. Work alone with eyes closed
   C. Run with the tool
   D. Wear safety gear and follow instructions

12. When learning Robotics, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Robotics.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Robotics.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Robotics.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Robotics.

13. When learning Data Structures, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Data Structures.
   B. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Data Structures.
   C. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Data Structures.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Data Structures.

14. When learning Cloud Computing, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Cloud Computing.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Cloud Computing.
   C. Skip safety briefings for Cloud Computing.
   D. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Cloud Computing.

15. A computer’s main brain for processing is the: (1 mark)
   A. Keyboard
   B. CPU
   C. Monitor
   D. Speaker

16. When learning Career Opportunities, the safest correct step is: (1 mark)
   A. Skip safety briefings for Career Opportunities.
   B. Leave sharp tools on the floor after Career Opportunities.
   C. Follow procedure, use tools correctly, and check safety for Career Opportunities.
   D. Guess wiring or cutting steps for Career Opportunities.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
17. In three clear sentences, explain Professional Ethics and Legal Issues in Computing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Network Troubleshooting and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Cybersecurity and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Cloud Computing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Social and Ethical Issues in Networking and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Data Structures and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
